q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis: NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is August 23, 2026. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release occurred on May 20, 2026 (per the research provided), which is in the **past**. This question appears to be asking about guidance that was already released nearly 3 months ago.

The guidance released was: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which corresponds to a range of $89.2B to $92.8B.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

Since the guidance has already been announced (May 20, 2026), the "most likely outcome" is simply the stated guidance: **$91.0 billion**.

NVIDIA explicitly provided this figure with a ±2% tolerance band. This is not a forecast of what they *will* announce—it's what they *did* announce. The current date (August 23, 2026) is well after the May 20 announcement.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

If this question is asking for what actual Q2 FY2027 *revenue* will be (not guidance), then downward factors might include:
- Macro weakness or reduced datacenter spending
- China restrictions impacting sales more than expected
- Competitive pressures from AMD or other vendors
- However, Q1 FY2027 already beat guidance by ~$2B, suggesting strong execution

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Continued datacenter momentum (Q1 beat guidance by $2B)
- Strong AI/accelerator demand
- Upward analyst revisions (research notes 5 recent upward revisions, 0 downward)
- The ±2% range allows for upside to $92.8B

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

Per the research: 
- NVIDIA Q1 FY2027 actual: **$81.6B** (beat guidance by ~$2B)
- NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 forward guidance: **$91.0B ± 2%** ($89.2B–$92.8B)
- Wall Street consensus near: **$91.9B**
- Guidance assumes zero Data Center compute revenue from China

---

## Reasoning

The research explicitly states that NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue was **$91.0 billion** with a ±2% tolerance, released May 20, 2026. This is a historical fact as of the current date (August 23, 2026).

If the question is asking "what will NVIDIA's forward guidance be" and that guidance was already released on May 20, 2026, then the answer is the stated guidance: $91.0 billion.

If the question is asking what Q2 FY2027 *actual reported revenue* will be (and "forward guidance" is shorthand for what they guided to), then we anchor on:
- The stated guidance: $91.0B ± 2%
- Recent outperformance: Q1 beat by ~$2B
- Analyst consensus: $91.9B (above midpoint but within range)
- Recent momentum: 5 upward analyst revisions, 0 downward

The range provided (99.5B to 115.5B) extends well above current guidance, but the historical data and guidance are in the $89–$93B range. This suggests the question may be testing whether I recognize that the guidance has already been announced, or whether I can project beyond it.

Given:
- Guidance is $91.0B with ±2% tolerance → $89.2B–$92.8B
- Q1 beat by ~$2B suggests upside bias
- Wall Street at $91.9B
- The question asks specifically about "forward guidance in Q2 FY2027 earnings release"—which already happened

The most defensible interpretation: **The forward guidance announced in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release was $91.0 billion.**

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, released on May 20, 2026, projected $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts, compiled by Yahoo! Finance, have an average estimate near $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This falls within NVIDIA's guided range, which has a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). In Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported $81.6 billion, exceeding its own guidance by approximately $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Analysts have also nudged their Q2 numbers higher, with five upward revisions and none down in the past month [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
